name: The Glimmer
summary: Magic in Vaeloria is the Glimmer: a broken echo of the creation-song, scattered when the Sundering shattered the Weavers' binding. It is rare, feared, and expensive — every working thins the Veil and greys the caster. This document consolidates how magic works, who can work it, what it costs, and how the realms govern it.

nature.what_it_is: A residue of the song of creation. Where the world's underlying music runs close to the surface — ruins, true places, cursed ground — it can be coaxed into effect. The Glimmer is not a force to be commanded but a melody to be borrowed.
nature.how_it_manifests: Workings announce themselves: a faint tone beneath hearing, a shimmer like heat-haze, a moment where colors sharpen. Witnesses report the sensation of a held breath. In the Burning Sands the Glimmer flickers visibly; in the Dusk Reach it moves like something walking under leaves.
nature.what_it_is_not: It is not divine favor — the gods withdrew before the Glimmer existed. It is not the song itself; the song is whole only in prophecy. Casting the Glimmer is whistling a fragment of a broken symphony.

the_cost.on_the_world: Every working feeds the thinning of the Veil. This is why magic is feared: the sum of all workings, mortal and Concord alike, tore the Quiet open once. The Backfiring of Solmere (183 AA) proved even small licensed magic carves local wounds.

on_the_caster.name: the Greying
on_the_caster.description: Each working takes a note from the caster's own aliveness. Colors dim around them. Food loses taste. Their voice flattens; their footsteps go quiet. Long-term casters become easy to pick out in a crowd: too-still people in a world of noise.

progression.sign: food tastes of little; mirrors seem slightly dull
voice flattens; animals grow wary; candlelight bends toward them
footsteps silent; shadows lag a half-beat; the caster stops dreaming
the caster barely registers to the senses — most at this stage walk into the Quiet 'of their own accord'

on_the_caster.reversal: Unknown. Rest slows it; nothing documented has undone it. The First-Heard sect claims the Waking's young Glimmerborn grey slower — evidence, they say, that the song is healing.

glimmerborn.who: Those born with the echo intact enough to hear and use. Not trained — born. The talent traces to Weaver bloodlines, proximity to true places, and chance; the Censer's birth-record watchlists exist because of the first two.
glimmerborn.waves: Glimmerborn appear in waves correlated with the Veil's thinning: many during the Silence's purges, near-none through the Grey Peace, and rising again since the Waking (~700 AA). Year 812 has seen more births than any year since Solmere.
glimmerborn.without_training: Untrained Glimmerborn work by instinct: small effects, unpredictable, often triggered by strong emotion. These 'wild notes' are what circle-tests are designed to catch.
glimmerborn.with_training: Given structure (Old Weaver craft or patient instinct), a Glimmerborn can work deliberately — but every deliberate working deepens the Greying. Most hedge-witches refuse to teach for exactly this reason.
glimmerborn.fate: In the Crownlands: taken by the Censer, and none return. In the deep-folk holds: turned out into the snow. In the Greenwood: the first, forbidden exile. In the sands: quietly ignored, if they are discreet.

traditions.name: Old Weaver Craft
traditions.summary: The Concord's tradition: structured workings taught through written Old Weaver notation. Precise, powerful, and exactly what the Edict of Silence bans. The Rememberers preserve it; the Censer burns it.
traditions.practitioners: Rememberers' cells, sealed colleges (if any survive), the Censer's own archive-wardens

traditions.name: Hedge-Craft
traditions.summary: Folk magic: charms, knots, spoken bargains with the echo. Weak, slow, and mostly harmless — coaxing rather than commanding. Common enough that every village has a hedge-witch; harmless enough that the Censer rarely bothers.
traditions.practitioners: Village hedge-witches, midwives, caravan charm-sellers (half of Ashveil Cross's stock is fake; half is worse)

traditions.name: Sanctioned Circle Work
traditions.summary: Workings performed inside warded circles under Censer observation: tests, containments, and the rare licensed working. Legal nowhere else. The Oath-Sept's certified cantrips for royal disputes are the Crownlands' one tiny lawful niche.

traditions.name: The Unbinding Path
traditions.summary: Ithyn's teaching: the song belongs to no institution. Its texts are the most hunted objects on Aurelith — a single genuine page sold in the Hollow Mile for a king's ransom in 812 AA.
traditions.practitioners: None openly. The Unbinding faction died in the Sundering; its texts did not.

traditions.name: The First-Heard Path
traditions.summary: A new tradition, barely a decade old: work with the returning Glimmer gently, treat each Glimmerborn as a musician not a prisoner. Its practitioners are incense-bearers within the Censer itself — which makes it either heresy or reform.

detection_and_law.circle_tests: The Censer's standard procedure: a suspect stands in a warded circle while a warden strikes a tuning-fork of Concord glass. If the echo answers — visible as a shimmer — the suspect is marked. False positives occur; quotas exist; this is known and unspoken.
detection_and_law.birth_records: Moonwardens keep the birth-ledgers the Censer cross-checks against Weaver bloodlines. Some wardens falsify entries; others report them.
detection_and_law.signs_anyone_can_see: The Greying's later stages are visible to any careful observer: too-quiet footsteps, dull mirrors, wariness of animals. Vigilance committees predate the Censer.

legal_status_by_realm.law: Edict of Silence (never repealed): written Old Weaver banned; Glimmerborn remanded to the Censer; certified cantrips witnessed by the Oath-Sept only
legal_status_by_realm.note: Solmere's fall (183 AA) created the Accords giving the Censer its modern warrant

legal_status_by_realm.law: Outright ban; the Glimmer is 'a lie the earth never made'. Glimmerborn are cast out into the snow
legal_status_by_realm.note: No exceptions recorded in four millennia

legal_status_by_realm.law: The Glimmer is a sickness on living things. A greenfolk who takes it suffers the first, forbidden exile
legal_status_by_realm.note: The Root-Wardens purge Glimmer-sickness from crops near the Quiet's edge

legal_status_by_realm.law: No formal ban; discretion is the law of the road
legal_status_by_realm.note: The sands' flickering Glimmer makes concealment easier; the Well-Sisters' only rule is do no harm to water

the_quiet.interaction: Within the Quiet, the Glimmer does not answer — castings simply fail, silently. Near its edge, workings behave strangely: delayed, doubled, or answered from the wrong direction.
the_quiet.the_backfiring_precedent: Solmere's harvest-blessing (183 AA) tore a pocket of Quiet beneath its own capital. Every serious magical accident since is measured against it.
the_quiet.answered_workings: Veil-Wardens record cases of workings near the edge receiving an answer no caster gave. The reports are filed, not investigated. No one wants to know what answers.

prophecy_tie: The Last Weaver prophecy (see cosmology.json) promises one born with the whole song, not the echo. The First-Heard sect believes the rising Glimmerborn waves are searching for that voice; the Nine Ashes believe the same thing and dread it.
adventure_hooks: Players witness a circle-test mark an obvious innocent and must decide whether quota-fraud is worth exposing mid-caravan.
A hedge-witch offers to teach a Glimmerborn player character — and shows her own greyed hands as the full price list.
A working near the Quiet's edge receives an answer. The Veil-Wardens will pay to know what shape it took.
The First-Heard sect asks players to smuggle a young Glimmerborn out of Ashveil Cross before the monthly barge — using a forged warrant bought from the Hollow Mile.
